correctness.rationale: The containment inequalities are z·n≤h−t. Below b²/a, h−t has nonnegative curvature measure. Above it, differentiating (h−t)/cos θ gives the sign of b²/h−t and the stated unique contact angle. Axial cones are bounded by nonnegative combinations of the two contact normals; the cosine support on each cone joins the remaining support C¹ and has zero curvature measure, whereas ρ−t is nonnegative on the retained arcs. This proves the true eroded support, not just a formal offset. The support-area formula gives the integral and the initial polynomial. Differentiating the support-area functional gives A′=−P_t: the t-derivative of support is −1 on active arcs and the curvature measure is zero on the cones. With u=θ_t, δ=t−b²/a=αu²+βu⁴+…, the u³ term of ∫₀ᵘ(ρ−t) cancels, and the u⁵ coefficient is 2α/15. Integration gives exactly +16α^(−3/2)/105 times δ^(7/2). Analyticity in u² gives the differentiated fractional expansion, C³ but not a fourth derivative. At t=b the vertical strip collapses and the horizontal intercept tends to zero; below b an open disk survives. The endpoint and the onset boundary recover b and a, and the disk case is immediate by radial erosion.
residual_risks: The published package's numerical diagnostics cover finite cases only; no numerical rerun, Lean verification or expert attestation was performed for this assessment.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the exact area distribution for the actual disk erosion of an unequal ellipse, with its explicit positive onset coefficient and inverse characterization. Formal offset cusps, general inner-parallel-body bounds, and the equal exponent for a different ellipse evolutoid loop do not cover that statement. Neither the Steiner polynomial below the threshold nor the general idea of using the medial axis is claimed as new.
residual_risks: An exact true-erosion formula or local coefficient may exist in specialized offset, medial-axis, or morphology literature; Matheron's original text was not verified. The assessment is based only on available inspected evidence.

value.rationale: The clearances are an intrinsic geometric probability observable. The exact formula identifies the valid post-focal boundary rather than integrating a self-intersecting formal offset; the cancellation leading to order 7/2 is a precise regularity boundary. One can also identify the two semiaxes from this one-dimensional law. These are useful exact facts about a standard convex body, not only its already-known initial Steiner regime.
residual_risks: No finite-sample stability estimate, analogous classification for general ovals, or uniform circular-limit estimate is inferred.
